use: Independent diagnostic goal injection only after main pipeline has not implemented the prespecified target; never used for main retrieval, judgment, generation, or primary success counts.
selection: Human, development-seen, target-informed diagnostic; not an automatic discovery claim.

goal.existing_validation: The original test asserts character=None for a non-shift modified printable shortcut without associated text. Another original test checks code 0 with associated text.
goal.missing_relation: Exercise a printable shortcut with at least one non-Shift modifier and nonempty associated text in the same legal Kitty event. Observe whether the shortcut still has no printable character.
goal.preconditions: Use an unshifted primary Unicode code point, not an uppercase primary to simulate Shift. Encode modifier parameter as 1 plus modifier bit flags: Shift=1, Alt=2, Ctrl=4. If Alt and Shift are both selected, the parameter is 4. Supply nonempty associated text in its protocol field. Use one fresh parser per complete sequence. The existing _keys helper feeds EOF after the sequence; never reuse that parser in a second _keys invocation.
goal.object_binding: One parsed Key event must carry both the selected shortcut modifiers and associated text. Keep the original parser fixture/helper boundary.
goal.operations: Construct one legal complete Kitty sequence containing both conditions. Feed that sequence through the original helper with a fresh parser. Inspect the resulting Key event.
goal.observation: Check the stable modifier-prefixed shortcut key, the corresponding sorted modifier tuple, and character=None on that same event.
goal.expectation: Non-Shift modified printable shortcuts retain stable shortcut names and character=None even when the terminal also reports associated text. Associated text must not create a printable shortcut character.
goal.oracle_basis: The public issue explicitly requires non-Shift modified printable shortcuts to keep modifier-prefixed names and character=None. Kitty protocol uses the unshifted primary code and a modifier bit field plus one; the original helper signals EOF after each sequence.

cases.alias_binding: Rebind only seed_alias/evidence_ids mechanically to the corresponding frozen run aliases by host_base_test_id; do not change goal semantics.

goal.existing_validation: The original runtime test resolves Recur through an outer pipe and applies readonly. It checks schema identity and output equality, but readonly does not change runtime values.
goal.missing_relation: Verify that resolving Recur preserves execution of a value-changing action in the OUTER pipe. Place the action after the object schema containing children: array(Recur), rather than only inside the value field schema.
goal.preconditions: Use the original public transform action. Choose a deterministic non-identity transformation that preserves the tree object shape and children field. Use legal finite input with a value that changes at the root and at least one recursive child. Keep string inputs within an unambiguous ASCII domain if using case conversion.
goal.object_binding: The object schema that contains the recursive child position must be the first item of the same outer pipe whose later transform action changes the current node value. recursive wraps that complete pipe.
goal.operations: Build the original object-and-Recur tree shape. Compose a pure value-changing action after the whole object schema. Wrap the complete pipeline with recursive. Parse finite nested input through the resulting schema.
goal.observation: Compare the concrete parsed output against the independently computed transformed root and child values. Runtime value changes, not only wrapper identity or an uncalled function type, must be asserted.
goal.expectation: The outer pipeline transformation executes on each parsed node, including the root and nodes reached through Recur. Output values follow the supplied transformation operation while the tree shape remains valid.
goal.oracle_basis: The public issue requires recursive composition to work correctly through pipe. The existing public transform action applies its operation to the runtime dataset value. The transformation operation itself determines each expected value; the submitted recursive implementation is not the oracle.
